    CHAPTER I

The measurements were first published in the spring of that year,
and the results[1] were at once disputed by several of his rivals.

A second series was undertaken in the following summer,[2] though
the weather was against the observers from beginning to end.

The third and last series[3] was never published in his lifetime.

Footnote 1: The second lecture of the Institute, delivered in May.

Footnote 2: The charitable bequests made in that year alone came
to a considerable sum, as the appendix shows in some detail.

Footnote 3: Read before the Society at a meeting in the School of
Economics, on Tuesday the fourteenth of February, at half past.
